policy: search for mature upstream tooling BEFORE writing custom code (project rule); custom code only fills gaps. Nothing here was installed with 'curl | sudo sh'. Distro packages preferred; clones go to tools/vendor/<tool> with the commit SHA recorded.
custom_code_that_remains_justified: armorx_lab transport + armorx_protocol (A5/A4 framing is vendor-specific; no upstream parser exists)
automated_scripts/parse-baseline.py, verify-key-id-map.py (device-specific decode of the 144-byte config)
automated_scripts/button-capture-harness.py (operator-synchronised capture; wraps the proven harness, does not reimplement BLE)

tools.name: bluez (bluetoothctl)
tools.purpose: BlueZ control CLI: pairing state, adapter info, GATT via D-Bus
tools.notes: used for adapter state checks; the primary path is Bumble on hci1

tools.name: bluez (btmgmt)
tools.purpose: mgmt API CLI: adapter index, address, powered state
tools.notes: used to resolve the lab adapter dynamically instead of hardcoding hci1

tools.name: bluez (btmon)
tools.purpose: kernel HCI monitor: canonical btsnoop evidence (capture path B)
tools.notes: cannot run concurrently with Bumble's HCI_USER_CHANNEL ownership of the same adapter; run it as a separate read-only session (path B) or via bluetoothd's own traffic

tools.name: wireshark/tshark
tools.purpose: decode btsnoop HCI captures and usbmon captures; protocol dissection
tools.privileges: dumpcap needs group/capabilities for live capture; offline decode is unprivileged
tools.notes: planned for the USB/F20 HID track and for reading btsnoop files; not yet exercised in this pass

tools.name: hid-tools (hid-recorder/hid-decode/hid-parse/hid-feature/hid-replay)
tools.purpose: HID report-descriptor decode, recording and replay from hidraw
tools.privileges: hidraw read often needs root or udev rules
tools.hardware: a hidraw device (F20 receiver / ArmorX in USB HID mode)
tools.notes: the single highest-value addition for the Linux-driver track; install when the F20/USB work starts rather than carrying it unused

tools.name: hidapitester (todbot)
tools.purpose: independent HID read/write probe, useful to cross-check our own HID send path
tools.install: not installed (build from source when needed)
tools.notes: cross-validation partner for our own HID code (two independent implementations, not two wrappers of one parser)

tools.name: usbhid-dump
tools.purpose: dump USB HID report descriptors without a driver
tools.notes: ready for the receiver enumeration step; gives raw descriptors for the report map

tools.name: usbmon + tshark
tools.purpose: URB-level USB capture of the vendor updater and of the receiver
tools.notes: capture only, no writes; will be used for the firmware-mode enumeration and the F20 init sequence

tools.name: pyusb / libusb
tools.purpose: programmatic USB access for a future userspace driver
tools.notes: can detach kernel drivers - only used deliberately, never on the composite Wi-Fi+BT adapter

tools.name: bumble
tools.purpose: pure-Python BLE stack used for the direct HCI-socket sessions (capture path A)
tools.privileges: root/CAP_NET_ADMIN for the HCI user channel
tools.notes: the interpreter must be /usr/bin/python3.14 (the venv python lacks socket.AF_BLUETOOTH); the py-bumble wrapper weds the two

tools.name: bleak (BlueZ/D-Bus GATT)
tools.purpose: independent GATT path through BlueZ for cross-validation of every GATT result
tools.notes: planned as the second, genuinely independent implementation for the GATT service dump (bumble vs bluetoothd)

tools.name: AC632Nuke
tools.hardware: JieLi AC63x target in bootrom mode
tools.notes: READ-ONLY identification only; no flash/erase/OTP commands under any circumstance this pass

tools.name: jl-misctools
tools.notes: safe: operates on copies of firmware files, never on hardware

tools.name: binwalk
tools.purpose: firmware image triage: magic, compression, containers
tools.install: not installed (7z/unzip/xxd cover part of this meanwhile)
tools.notes: would help the JLFS/uboot.boot hunt; install only if a firmware image actually appears

tools.name: ghidra / rizin / radare2
tools.purpose: static analysis of updater binaries and any firmware dump
tools.notes: deferred: no binary is under analysis yet; objdump+strings are enough for the current static searches

tools.name: kaitai struct
tools.purpose: declarative binary format specs (good fit for a future .axprofile format)
tools.notes: the 144-byte config layout is already documented in parse-baseline.py; a .ksy could replace it later, not now

tools.name: kagaimiq/jl-uboot-tool
tools.risk: CRITICAL - write/erase, and BD19/AC632N support is historically UNKNOWN
tools.notes: excluded from this pass by project rule: no write/erase, and an unverified loader must not be pointed at the device
